rows.author: J008
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE UNANG YAKAP CAMPAIGN, ADOPTING THE PROTOCOL ON ESSENTIAL NEWBORN CARE
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the disturbing trend in neonatal mortality by institutionalizing the Unang Yakap campaign which advocates the Essential Intrapartum Newborn Care ( E I N C ), a concept fully supported by W H O, describes by D O H as a series of time - bound and evidence - based interventions in caring for newborn babies and their mothers and therefore has a potential to decrease newborn death by at least half.

Involves non-costly simple ways or steps to improve health care services for babies during the first critical hours; and aims to train frontline maternal and newborn healthcare practitioners and educate pregnant women of the importance of observing the Unang Yakap protocol.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2020-02-04

rows.author: J008
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF ACTS CONSTITUTING SEXUAL HARASSMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBER 7877, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"SEXUAL HARASSMENT ACT OF 1995\"
rows.abstract:
Seeks to fill many gaps needed to address the limitation of the law and its provision which presupposes the existence of authority, influence or moral ascendancy between the offender and the offended party, by providing that a \"harasser\" could be anyone including a colleague or subordinate staff.

Proposes to strengthen the law by amending certain provisions so that \"sexual harassment\" now constitutes:
a) acts that are not only physical or verbal in nature, but also those committed using electronic devices or any available technology or means; b) acts that have been committed either within or outside the place of employment, training or education; and c) offensive remarks about a person's sexual orientation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2020-02-04

rows.author: J008
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING THE CRIME OF CYBER-BULLYING
rows.abstract:
Seeks to protect every citizen from cruelty in the virtual world by defining the scope of \" cyber - bullying \" and imposing penal sanctions to encourage netizens to be responsible and accountable for their cyber - actions.

Enumerates the \"acts of cruelty committed using the internet or any form of electronic media or technology that has the effect of stripping one's dignity or causing reasonable fear of  physical or emotional harm . . . \" which involves: repeatedly sending offensive, rude, and insulting messages; distributing derogatory information; posting/sending offensive photos; using the victim's virtual identity to send embarrassing materials; revealing and sharing personal or embarrassing information; and repeatedly sending messages that include threats of harm or online activities that cause fear on the victim's safety.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2020-02-04

rows.author: I089
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE AGRICULTURAL AND RURAL FINANCING SYSTEM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the shortcomings of agricultural and rural sectors´ credit extension which has been elusive due to failure of the market to allocate resources in an equitable manner, resulting to majority of them unable to earn enough as advanced farming technologies are inaccessible to them and their financial requirements to boost productivity are often unserved.

Provides a framework where automatic eligibility is granted with Phil. Guarantee Corp., Phil. Crop Insurance Corp. P C I C, Agricultural Credit and Policy Council ( A C P C ) and other governmental agencies providing services towards risk - mitigation in the agriculture sector.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CALAMITY FUND, TO AUGMENT DISASTER RESPONSE AND RECOVERY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Proposes to mandate LGUs to contribute one percent (1%) of their total revenues taken from the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund ( L D R R M F ) other than the amount set aside for the quick response fund; provided that an LGU who availed of the Fund shall contribute two percent (2%) of their L D R R M F for the next year; provided further, that the LGU shall revert to the one percent (1%) contribution if it did not avail of the Fund for the previous year.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA FOR MEDIA PROFESSIONALS

and their organizations.

Seeks to mandate that media professionals/journalists on field assignments shall be covered by additional insurance benefits as well as a corresponding hazard pay.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE AIRING OF ADVERTISEMENTS OF SUGAR SWEETENED BEVERAGES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract:
Seeks regulation in all media platforms such as radio, television and cable television, film and movies, online social media, electronic, print or whatever form of mass media, including outdoor advertisements, but not limited to signs and billboards.

Defines \"Sugar Sweetened Beverages ( S S B )\" to non-alcoholic beverages of any constitution (liquid, powder, or concentrates) that are pre-packaged and sealed in accordance with the F D A standards, that contain caloric and/or non-caloric sweeteners added by the manufacturers, and shall include, but not limited to the following: sweetened juice drinks; sweetened tea; all carbonated beverages; flavored water; energy and sports drinks; other powdered drinks not classified as milk, juice, tea, and coffee; cereal and grain beverages; and other non-alcoholic beverages that contain added sugar.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL ELECTRONIC TOLL COLLECTION SYSTEM FOR ALL EXPRESSWAYS IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish the interoperability of existing toll operations between different expressways to harness the full potential of providing fast, seamless and convenient means of land transportation.

Defines several terms among others such as Electronic Toll Interoperability which refers to a system where an 
electronic or R F I D tag from one toll road operator can be used in the toll road of another operator, or a single electronic of R F I D tag can be used to access all toll roads in the country.

Also refers Radio Frequency Identification or R F I D to a technology whereby digital data encoded in R F I D tags or labels are automatically identified, collected and entered into computer systems with little or no human intervention.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2020-02-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROTECTING CONSUMERS AND MERCHANTS ENGAGED IN INTERNET TRANSACTIONS, CREATING FOR THIS PURPOSE THE ECOMMERCE BUREAU AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to create an environment founded on trust among consumers and merchants, as a means to increase the number of eCommerce participants, and ultimately achieve sustainable growth.

Aims to address the need to establish an eCommerce Bureau under the Dept. of Trade and Industry ( D T I ) that: 1) will be given the responsibility to carry out the provisions of this bill; 2) will ensure the implementation of the Electronic Commerce Act of 2000 (R.A.NO.8792); and will be the focal point in the monitoring and implementation of the Phil. eCommerce roadmap.

Proposes that the sale or exchange of digital products shall include the following:
internet retail of consumer goods; online travel services; digital media providers; ride hailing services for personal transport; and financial services offered through digital online platforms.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE CITIES AND COMMUNITIES IN THE COUNTRY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Intends to address extreme poverty and inequality brought about by the rapid growth of cities, coupled with increasing rural to urban migration in line with the country's commitment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals ( S D Gs ).

Provides a model for sustainable cities and communities for existing ones by ensuring access to safe and affordable housing, upgrading highly dense slum settlements, investing in public transport, creating green public spaces and improving urban planning through inclusive and participatory management.

States the N E D A shall set targets based on several indicators to determine if a city or community has fully transitioned into a sustainable one: urban population living in slums; public transport access; protecting cultural heritage; economic losses, deaths and injuries from natural disasters; solid waste management and urban air pollution, open and safe spaces in cities, urban and regional planning; integrated and local disaster risk management.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2020-02-05

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PROTECTION TO FREELANCERS, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the limited rights of freelancers to associate and form organizations leading to a lack of standards on contracts, fees and work metrics by giving them same treatment as any other traditional laborer.

Aims to provide protection to freelancers by setting the standard requirements in terms of written contracts and payment of salaries between the employer and the freelancer.

Defines several terms among others such as \"Freelance worker\" which refers to any natural person or a One Person Corporation registered with the S E C, or registered as a sole proprietorship with the D T I, or registered as self - employed with the B I R, that is hired or retained as an independent contractor by a hiring party to provide services in exchange for compensation.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING BANKING INSTITUTIONS TO STRENGTHEN THE FINANCING SYSTEM FOR AGRICULTURAL, FISHERIES AND RURAL DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Mandating Banking Institutions To Strengthen The Financing System For Agricultural, Fisheries And Rural Development In The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Aims to promote rural development by enhancing access of rural communities and agricultural and fisheries households to financial services and programs that increase productivity, enhance market efficiency, promote modernization and improve the welfare and economic prospects of  beneficiaries in rural communities through active participation of banking institutions.

States that agricultural, fisheries and rural development financing shall consist of loans, investments and grants to finance activities identified under the Agro-Industry Modernization Credit and Financing Program (AMCFP) as enumerated under Chapter 3, Section 23 of RA 8435, off-farm/fishery activities, agricultural mechanization/modernization, agri-tourim, green finance projects, acquisition of lands under the Agrarian Reform Code of the Philippines and its amendments, efficient and effective marketing, processing, distribution and storage of agricultural and fishery commodities, public rural infrastructure, as well as programs that shall address the development needs of rural communities, and all other activities as may be determined by the Agricultural and Fisheries and Capacity-Building Council (AFFCC).

Mandates all banking institutions, except newly-established banks for a period of five (5) years from the date of commencement of the bank´s operations, shall set aside a credit quota, or a minimum mandatory agricultural and fisheries financing requirement of at least twenty-five percent (25%) of their total loanable funds as defined by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP).
rows.alias_name: “Rural Agricultural and Fisheries Development Financing System Act.”
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT RA11901 (Lapsed into law on 2022-07-28)

rows.author: I070
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE FISCAL REGIME FOR THE MINING INDUSTRY
rows.title_short: Establishing The Fiscal Regime For The Mining Industry
rows.abstract:
Aims to rationalize and institute a single fiscal regime applicable to all mineral agreements for a better revenue sharing between the mining industry and the government.Creates the Natural Resource Trust Fund from the revenue collected from the margin-based royalty paid by the large-scale metallic mining operations outside of mineral reservations that shall redound to the benefit of provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays directly affected by mining operations. 

Provides the following key provisions: 1.) Impose a three percent (3%) royalty tax on large-scale mining operations located within mining reservation areas; 2.) Impose a margin-based royalty tax on large-scale mining operations outside mining reservation areas ranging from 1% to 5%, as the case may be; 3.) Impose a royalty tax on small-scale mining operations equivalent to one-tenth of one percent (1/10 of 1%) of gross output; and 4.) Impose an additional margin-based tax on windfall profits gained from mining operations ranging from 1% to 10%, as the case may be.

Exempts mining contractors for all metallic and non-metallic mining operations from the confidentiality clauses of the National Internal Revenue Code  of 1977, as amended, including Sec. 270 in relation to Sec. 71 therein, by requiring  them to observe fiscal transparency and comply with the requirements of the Executive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI) of government.Creates the Natural Resource Trust Fund from the revenue collected from the margin-based royalty paid by the large-scale metallic mining operations outside of mineral reservations that shall redound to the benefit of provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays directly affected by mining operations.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ENCOURAGING CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Encouraging Corporate Social Responsibility, Providing Incentives Therefor
rows.abstract:
Refers corporate social responsibility (CSR) to the commitment of business to contribute on a voluntary basis to sustainable economic development by working with relevant stakeholders to improve their lives in ways that are good for business, sustainable development agenda and society at large.

Defines CSR-related activities as charitable programs and projects; scientific research; youth and sports development; cultural or educational promotion; services to veterans and senior citizens; social welfare; environmental sustainability; health development; disaster relief and assistance; and employee and worker welfare related related CSR activities.

Allows stock corporations to retain surplus profits in excess of one hundred per cent (100%) of their paid-in capital stock to be used to definite corporate expansion or corporate social responsibility projects and programs approved by the directors.

Mandates the Department of Trade and Industry to recognize and reward all business organizations for outstanding, innovative and world-class CSR-related services, projects and programs , and extend endorsement and encouragements to domestic and foreign corporations doing business in the Philippines which are candidates for recognition in international award-giving bodies for their CSR-related activities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AND ENHANCING THE ROLE OF PARENT-TEACHER AND COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS IN PROMOTING THE WELFARE AND PROTECTING THE RIGHTS OF CHILDREN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 603, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE CHILD AND YOUTH WELFARE CODE\"
rows.title_short: Institutionalizing And Enhancing The Role Of Parent - Teacher And Community Associations In Promoting The Welfare And Protecting The Rights Of Children
rows.abstract:
Aims to encourage the building of strong family ties as well as responsive, responsible and stable community ties to promote the welfare, protect the rights and enhance opportunities for children and the youth.

Allows PTCAs to create a program for children  to ensure that they become well-rounded, stable, sociable and civic-oriented citizens; ensure the full cooperation of parents, teachers, and other community stakeholders; consult the children at all times; serve as an avenue for local school stakeholders to design other appropriate programs that will address children´s concerns; raise awareness on and support the implementation of child protection policies as mandated by DepEd; assess the local implementation of basic education program; partner with the appropriate school officials and student councils in the design and implementation of basic education school programs; and strengthen accountability among school stakeholders by facilitating information dissemination among parents in the community on DepEd and local school programs and services.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2020-05-20, transmitted to the Senate on 2020-05-21 and received by the Senate on 2020-05-21

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF FINANCIAL CONSUMERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to address the travails (fraud, abuse and misconduct) being experienced by financial consumers due to the rapid development of complex financial products coupled with the use of advanced technologies.

Proposes therefore to ensure that the rights of each and every consumer are protected by providing, among others, financial regulators such as the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Insurance Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Defines several terms among others which include \"Financial Consumer\" who is a recipient of \"Financial Products or Services\" which are developed or marketed by a Financial Service Provider which may include, but are not limited to savings, credit, insurance, investments, payments, remittances and other similar products and services; also includes digital financial services.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA FOR PUBLIC COUNSELORS
rows.abstract:
Seeks to protect, promote, advance and develop the ethical, socio - economic well - being, and career and professional development of the guidance counselors, their living and working conditions and terms of employment in the public schools and in the government service.

Aims to achieve the right of the students to avail the guidance and counselling services in the schools; strengthen the Mental Health Act(R.A.No.11036); help to adequately address the mental, emotional and developmental needs of the basic education learners and clients; remove the emotional, behavioral, and psycho-social barriers to learning; support school staff, teachers and administrators in improving classroom management through the conduct of behavioral and other guidance related interventions, among others.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR CREATIVE INDUSTRY WELFARE PROTECTION
rows.abstract:
Refers \"Creative Worker\" to any person who performs work requiring invention, imagination, administration,
coordination, originality, or talent in a recognized field of artistic or creative endeavor, such as but not limited to music, writing, acting, and the graphic arts, whether or not he or she is bound by any relations
of employment or association.

Enumerates the rights and privileges of an accredited creative worker such as social protection, including but not limited to S S S / G S I S, PagI B I G, PhilHealh; accident insurance which involve hazardous work; standard working hours which shall vary according to age; workplace safety and health hazards risk reduction; synchronized medical and safety precautionary measures; second / alternative careers; and artist´s village among others.

Specifies the role of the National Commission for Culture and Arts ( N C C A ) which shall create a Creative Workers' Welfare Office to implement the provisions of this Act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07762

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 3, 8, AND 9 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9856, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS \"THE REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUST (REIT) ACT OF 2009\"
rows.abstract:
Intends to ensure that the funds invested through the \"Real Estate Investment Act of 2009\" enacted to promote the development of the capital market to fund infrastructure projects and further improve the real estate industry, are to be reinvested in the Philippines to secure full domestic participation in the real estate industry.

Defines the terms \"REINVESTMENT PLAN\" and provides that any proceeds realized by the sponsor/promoter from the sale of R E I T share or other securities issued in exchange for income - generating real estate transferred to R E I T and any money raised by the sponsor/promoter from the sale of any of its income - generating to the R E I T, in any real estate including any redevelopment thereof, and/or infrastructure projects in the country, must be reinvested in the Philippines.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER STRENGTHEN THE ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING LAW, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING ACT OF 2001, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Aims to implement plan to include legal framework addressing money laundering, terrorism financing, proliferation of financing weapons of mass destruction, and the framework for supervision of financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses and professions.

Introduces therefore several amendments to Republic Act No.9160, as amended which includes:
a) inclusion of real estate agents as covered persons; b) inclusion of tax crimes and violation of the Strategic Trade Management Act which indirectly includes proliferation of weapons of mass destruction as a predicate offenses to money laundering; c) enhancement of the investigative powers of the A M L C; d) authority of the A M L C to implement targeted financial sanctions on proliferation financing; e) prohibition on the issuance of injunctive relief against freeze orders and forfeiture proceedings; f) and retention of portion of forfeited assets.

rows.author: I083
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE CONGRESSIONAL OVERSIGHT COMMITTEE ON THE NATIONAL BUDGET
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the issues of pork barrel, Priority Development Assistance Fund ( P D A F ), Disbursement Acceleration Program ( D A P ), and other similar discretionary funds which expose the problems and weaknesses of the actual budget process that took away huge amount of public funds intended for social services for the people.

Proposes to strengthen Congress oversight function in the budget process to enhance the effectiveness of the national budget towards the country's development goals and people's well-being, thereby creating a strong, permanent oversight committee with defined powers.

rows.author: I091
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 236 AND 237 (A), (B), OF CHAPTER IV, TITLE I, BOOK II, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract:
Aims to impose additional Ad Valorem tax on idle lands at the rate of five percent (5%) intended to disincentivized  the owners whose lands, many remained undeveloped, much less utilized.

Provides for the coverage of idle lands, and those that should NOT be considered idle as follows:

a) Agricultural lands planted WITH VEGETABLE OR FRUIT BEARING CROPS OR with at least TWO HUNDRED (200)
trees to a hectare, OR A PROPORTIONATE NUMBER OF TREES IF SUCH LAND IS EITHER LESS THAN OR MORE THAN ONE HECTARE; and

b) LANDS PLANTED WITH AT LEAST ONE (1) TREE FOR EVERY FIFTY (50) SQUARE METERS, OR AT LEAST FIFTY PERCENT (50%) OF THE AREA IS PLANTED WITH VEGETABLE OR FRUIT BEARING CROPS FOR A PERIOD OF AT LEAST SIX (6) MONTHS IN A YEAR.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2020-02-10

rows.author: J021
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE TREATMENT AND RESEARCH INSTITUTE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to establish a hospital that would specialize in the treatment of infectious diseases like the Middle East Respiratory Syndrome ( M E R S ), Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome ( S A R S ),  and the Novel Coronavirus Acute Respiratory Diseases (2019-n Co V  A R D ).

Provides for the following objectives of the Institute among others, as regards to: mobilization of healthcare and security personnel and resources; isolation and quarantine operations; safe transportation and ensuring minimum contact with other persons; ensuring compliance with orders for isolation and restriction of movement; decontamination of equipment, supplies and personnel of infected persons; imposition of travel restrictions; primary repository of all database for researchers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2020-02-10

rows.author: J021
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION OF EMPLOYEES IN THE BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING (BPO) INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Aims to maintain a balance between the protection of the interests and welfare of the workers and employees in the B P O industry and to ensure that the impact of its growth be trickled down to most of the populations.

Enumerates several rights of B P O employees as regards to organizing/joining labor organizations; safe and
healthy working environment; an hour meal break; respect for privacy when it comes to personal phone calls, in compliance with the Data Privacy Act; comfortable resting area for night shift employees until daybreak;
and to be informed of the terms and conditions of their contract.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2020-02-10

rows.author: J012
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESERVING THE INDIGENOUS GAMES OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Preserving The Indigenous Games Of The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Aims to recognize and promote the rights of indigenous cultural communities through the preservation of the indigenous peoples´ games thereby strengthening their self-expression, and promote peace, harmony, goodwill and camaraderie among them.

Mandates the Philippine Sports Commission (PSC), in coordination with the Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) and the local government units (LGUs) to conduct annual regional and national indigenous sports competitions.

rows.author: F073
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE DELINEATION OF THE SPECIFIC FOREST LIMITS OF THE PUBLIC DOMAIN AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Providing For The Delineation Of The Specific Forest Limits Of The Public Domain
rows.abstract: Provides guidelines and procedures to be followed in determining the specific limits of forest lands; Creates the National Review and Evaluation Committee to process, evaluate and approve all completed assessment and delineation reports; Mandates that the final forest line determined and established by the DENR shall be the final forest land boundary of the country  which shall not be diminished nor reduced except by an Act of Congress.  Creates the Land Classification Conflict Adjudication Board to resolve controversies arising from land classification as a result of the delimitation of forest lands.
rows.status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2020-05-14
